record.reason: The paper re-examines BERT/RoBERTa pruning on SMC-Benchmark. On BERT encoder CPU inference with DeepSparse, pruning embeddings/classification head gave negligible speedups even at 98% sparsity and could damage accuracy; it recommends pruning the encoder. It also finds large initial pruning steps (50–70%) and adjusted schedules improve recovery at 90–97% sparsity. Scope is encoder classification/fine-tuning rather than generative LLM serving, so this is reasoned borderline.
record.title: How to Prune Your Language Model: Recovering Accuracy on the "Sparsity May Cry" Benchmark
